reasons: Open-fields no-protection rule stated correctly; Hester (open fields, 265 U.S. 57) and Oliver (No-Trespassing signs/fences do not convert open fields, 466 U.S. 170) are the correct anchors; Dunn four-factor curtilage line accurately invoked.
Waiver/invocation rule correct: Edwards bar-to-reinterrogation on counsel invocation; Elstad/Seibert/Patane correctly named as the Miranda-fruits line. No mis-attribution.
Third-party doctrine (Smith/Miller) and Carpenter (2018) narrow CSLI limit stated accurately, including that Carpenter did not overrule Smith or Miller.
Collective-knowledge/fellow-officer imputation rule accurately stated (pools, never manufactures, basis-in-fact required); no citation to mis-verify.

Watson (warrantless public arrest on PC), Atwater (fine-only offense), Devenpeck (objective; offense need not be the one named), Virginia v. Moore (state-law violation is not a 4A violation) all correctly stated and cited; Payton threshold caveat correct.
Birchfield holding correct (breath test yes, blood test needs warrant/consent/exigency); Schmerber/McNeely/Mitchell dissipating-alcohol line correctly named; 579 U.S. 438 accurate.
Garrity coerced-statement immunity correctly stated; Garrity 385 U.S. 493 and Lefkowitz v. Turley 414 U.S. 70 are correct anchors.
Implied-license knock-and-talk framework is exactly Jardines (within license = no search, exceeding = search); King correctly cited for permissibility of the knock-and-talk itself.
Nieves PC-defeats-retaliatory-arrest rule and its similarly-situated-comparator exception correctly stated; Gonzalez v. Trevino (2024) correctly cited as the follow-on clarifying the exception.

Terry quotes ('specific reasonable inferences...','inchoate and unparticularized suspicion or hunch') and Cortez quotes ('particularized and objective basis','the whole picture') correctly attributed with pincites 27 and 417-18.
Two-step reasonableness framework accurate; Hicks (moving stereo to read serial number is a search) correctly cited at 480 U.S. 321.
Graham v. Connor objective-reasonableness standard for excessive-force-in-seizure claims correctly stated and cited (490 U.S. 386).
Voluntary-abandonment/loss-of-REP rule correctly stated (Katz standard, must be voluntary, not product of unlawful conduct); Greenwood 486 U.S. 35 is the correct anchor.
Gerstein prompt-PC (informal, non-adversarial) and McLaughlin 48-hour presumption with burden-shift and no weekend excuse correctly stated and cited.
Automobile exception (ready mobility + PC, no separate exigency, reaches containers) correctly stated; Carroll 267 U.S. 132 and Acevedo 500 U.S. 565 correct anchors.
Tent/temporary-dwelling REP proposition is a coherent, uncited framing consistent with Katz (context of pitch controls, not permanence); no over-claim of a holding.
residual_risks: Uncited synthesis; no controlling SCOTUS tent case exists, so it rests on the Katz framework rather than a squarely-on-point holding.

reasons: Ciraolo (fixed-wing 1,000 ft), Florida v. Riley (plurality, helicopter 400 ft), Dow Chemical (aerial photography of industrial site), and Kyllo (sense-enhancing tech not in general public use revealing home interior) all correctly stated and cited.
Hiibel stop-and-identify (4A reasonably-related, 5A unless name itself incriminating, duty from state law) and Kolender void-for-vagueness limit correctly stated and cited.

Excessive-Fines constraint on civil in rem forfeiture (Timbs incorporation, Bajakajian gross-disproportionality) plus due-process and no-constitutional-innocent-owner-defense correctly stated; Culley v. Marshall (2024) correctly cited on procedural timing.
Federal subjective entrapment test (inducement + lack of predisposition, predisposition controls) correctly stated; Sorrells 287 U.S. 435 and Sherman 356 U.S. 369 correct anchors.
Katz overruling Olmstead, Berger particularity, Title III codification (18 U.S.C. sec. 2510-2522), Keith domestic-security-warrant rule, and FISA for foreign intelligence all correctly stated.

Fire-scene rule (burning building exigency, reasonable post-blaze investigation, later entries need administrative or criminal warrant) correctly stated; Tyler 436 U.S. 499 and Clifford 464 U.S. 287 (plurality) correct anchors.

Black-letter framing is cautious and internally coherent: geofence-as-general-warrant is 'unsettled', 5th Cir. Smith (110 F.4th 817) held them general warrants, SCOTUS declined the categorical rule leaving PC/particularity live on remand; no disclosed contradiction.
The asserted 2026 SCOTUS Chatrie disposition post-dates my knowledge and no case text is inlined, so I cannot independently confirm the holding characterization from the disclosed registry alone.
residual_risks: Existence and exact holding of Chatrie v. United States (2026, SCOTUS) — and that it 'expressly declined' the categorical rule — cannot be confirmed from disclosed evidence; verification requires the S2/CL lake record. Load-bearing node, so a currency check on the remand posture is warranted.

reasons: Correctly states there is no controlling SCOTUS decision and frames the in-home-location warrant requirement as an analogical inference from Karo (interior fact) and Kyllo; DOJ/DHS 2015 warrant policy accurately described. No over-claim of a holding.
residual_risks: The 'is a search requiring a warrant' conclusion is a doctrinal inference, not a holding; the node itself flags the absence of controlling authority.

reasons: QI standard (clearly-established right a reasonable person would know) and Pearson either-order discretion (relaxing Saucier) correctly stated; Harlow 457 U.S. 800 and Pearson 555 U.S. 223 correct anchors.

Jacobsen 'meaningful interference with possessory interests' definition quoted accurately with pincite 113; Soldal v. Cook County correctly cited for seizure-of-property independent of privacy; search/seizure-distinct point correct.

Functional-approach absolute immunity correctly stated: Imbler (prosecutorial advocacy), Rehberg (grand-jury/trial witness incl. police), Buckley (investigative/complaining-witness conduct gets only QI). All anchors correct.
Suspicionless highway-safety (sobriety) checkpoint upheld under programmatic balancing; Sitz 496 U.S. 444 is the correct anchor.

Fruit-of-poisonous-tree (not but-for; exploitation vs. means sufficiently distinguishable) is verbatim Wong Sun; Brown v. Illinois three attenuation factors (temporal proximity, intervening circumstances, purpose/flagrancy) correctly stated and cited.
Private-search (Burdeau/Jacobsen/Walter, government may not exceed scope) and extraterritorial nonresident-alien limit ('the people', Verdugo-Urquidez) correctly stated and cited.
Special-needs framework (reasonableness balance in lieu of warrant/PC when a need beyond ordinary law enforcement is served) accurately stated; uncited but a correct doctrinal summary.
Wilson (knock-and-announce part of reasonableness), Richards (case-specific reasonable suspicion, no blanket crime-category exception), and Hudson (no exclusionary remedy) correctly stated and cited.

Sec. 1983/Bivens divide, 'disfavored judicial activity' with the single-reason-to-pause bar (Egbert/Abbasi), and the FTCA waiver-with-exceptions-and-judgment-bar all correctly stated; Bivens 403 U.S. 388 and Egbert 596 U.S. 482 correct anchors.

Terry stop (RAS of criminal activity) and separate-suspicion protective frisk (armed and presently dangerous, outer-clothing pat-down) correctly stated; Terry 392 U.S. 1 and Adams v. Williams 407 U.S. 143 correct anchors.
Buie two-tier protective sweep (adjoining spaces without suspicion; beyond on reasonable articulable suspicion) correctly stated and cited (494 U.S. 325).

Gant two prongs (unsecured arrestee within reaching distance, or reason to believe vehicle contains evidence of offense of arrest) correctly stated; Belton automatic rule correctly described as replaced; 556 U.S. 332 correct.

Routine border searches need no warrant/PC/suspicion (Ramsey) and non-routine highly intrusive searches need at least reasonable suspicion; Flores-Montano correctly cited for the routine end. Anchors correct.

Jones two-part trespass test (physical intrusion on protected area + to obtain information) at 404-05 and the 'added to, not substituted for' quote at 409 correctly attributed; Silverman correctly cited for intrusion-need-not-be-state-law-trespass.

Gates four-corners/fair-probability/totality standard and veracity-plus-basis-of-knowledge, plus Ventresca deferential substantial-basis/commonsense (not hypertechnical) review, correctly stated and cited.
Exclusionary rule as case-in-chief bar on evidence and its fruits, and as a judicially created deterrent remedy (not a personal right), correctly stated; Weeks/Mapp/Calandra correct anchors.

Proof-ladder synthesis correct: hunch authorizes nothing, RAS -> stop/frisk, PC -> arrest/full search/warrant, trial burdens (preponderance/clear-and-convincing/BRD) are conviction standards; Terry/Gates/Brinegar correctly cited for the field standards.

Core constructive-entry rule (coercing a suspect out of a surrounded home is a Payton in-home arrest; arrestee's location fixes where arrest occurs; voluntary door-opening not protected; complete perimeter defeats flight exigency) is sound doctrine, and the 9th Cir. anchors (Nora, Al-Azzawy, Vaneaton) are correctly applied.
residual_risks: The precise circuit-split roster (2d/6th/9th/10th recognizing; 5th/7th/11th narrow; 1st/3d/4th/8th unmapped) and the exact F.3d/F.2d pincites cannot be independently confirmed from disclosed evidence; a treatment/currency check on the circuit alignment is warranted.

reasons: Neutral-and-detached-magistrate requirement correctly stated: Johnson ('competitive enterprise of ferreting out crime'), Lo-Ji Sales (joining the search operation), Coolidge (prosecutorial stake), and Connally (fee for issuing but not denying) are the correct anchors.
Riley rule correct: SIA does not reach cell-phone digital contents; officers may seize and inspect physical aspects but need a warrant to search data; 573 U.S. 373 at 403 correct.
Sec. 1983 color-of-law cause of action (Monroe v. Pape) and Monell municipal liability limited to official policy/custom, no respondeat superior, correctly stated and cited.
Leon good-faith (objectively reasonable reliance on warrant/statute/ordinance/record) and its four failure situations correctly stated; Leon 468 U.S. 897 and Herring 555 U.S. 135 correct anchors.
Thompson v. Clark (favorable termination = ended without conviction) and Chiaverini (probable cause assessed charge by charge) correctly stated and cited for the 4A malicious-prosecution analog.
Miranda warnings gate (silence, use against, counsel/appointed-if-indigent) and case-in-chief inadmissibility absent warnings+valid waiver correctly stated; 384 U.S. 436 correct.
Due-process suggestiveness/reliability-under-totality rule (Manson v. Brathwaite) and post-attachment corporeal-lineup counsel right (Wade) correctly stated and cited.
Container/luggage rule correct: Chadwick footlocker warrant requirement limited by Acevedo for a container found in a vehicle where PC as to the container permits on-the-spot search.

SIA-persons rule correct: full search of arrestee's person on lawful custodial arrest without separate PC (Robinson) plus wingspan/immediate-control area (Chimel at 763); pincites 235 and 763 correct.
Four warrant requisites (PC, particular place, particular things, neutral magistrate on oath) and Leon good-faith-with-floors correctly summarized; no over-claim.

Due-process voluntariness (totality; official coercion overbearing the will; conditions/threats-promises/individual characteristics; no single factor dispositive) correctly stated; official-coercion predicate is consistent with Connelly. Uncited but accurate.
